title: CRISPR activation for SCN2A-related neurodevelopmental disorders
perturbation: Plasmid transfection of CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) targeting the Scn2a promoter vs control in Neuro2a cells
incidental_ifn_note: Plasmid DNA transfection carrying CRISPRa machinery into cultured cells introduces cytosolic nucleic acids that incidentally activate type-I interferon / ISG responses.
evidence: The record investigates mRNA expression after CRISPR activation targeting the mouse Scn2a promoter in Neuro2a cells for therapeutic modeling of neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Differential gene expression in spinal cords from uninfected WT mice and infected RdRP transgenic mice (2 days post infection with Encephalomyocarditis Virus, EMCV)
perturbation: Encephalomyocarditis Virus (EMCV) infection (2 days post-infection) in RdRP transgenic mice vs uninfected wild-type mice
evidence: The GEO record profiles gene expression in mouse spinal cords to analyze the antiviral effect of a picornaviral RdRP transgene against EMCV infection.

title: Differential gene expression in spinal cords from WT mice during uninfected (baseline) conditions and after (2 days post) infection with Encephalomyocarditis Virus (EMCV)
perturbation: Encephalomyocarditis Virus (EMCV) infection (2 days post-infection) vs uninfected baseline in wild-type mice
evidence: The GEO record measures transcriptome changes in wild-type mouse spinal cords 2 days post-infection with Encephalomyocarditis Virus (EMCV).

title: Next Generation Sequencing Facilitates Quantitative Analysis of brain Transcriptome after viral infection with ZIKV (Zika Virus)
perturbation: Zika virus (ZIKV) infection at E14.5 vs uninfected control
evidence: The study profiles RNA-seq changes in E17.5 mouse brains following Zika virus infection, demonstrating significant activation of viral immune response pathways.

title: RNA editing is the essential function of ADAR1 and, in the absence of MDA5, is dispensable for normal adult homeostasis [RNAseq (Fetal Brain)]
perturbation: ADAR1 editing-deficient point mutation (E861A) vs wild-type in fetal brain
incidental_ifn_note: Loss of ADAR1 RNA editing leads to unedited endogenous dsRNA accumulation, which activates cytosolic dsRNA sensor MDA5 and drives a strong type-I interferon response.
evidence: The study shows that ADAR1 A-to-I RNA editing essentiality is mediated by preventing endogenous dsRNA from triggering the MDA5 cytosolic RNA sensor and interferon pathways.

title: Lysophosphatidylserines derived from microbiota in Crohn’s disease elicit pathological Th1 response
tissue_cell: colonic CD4+ T cells (naive, effector, regulatory T cells)
perturbation: Lysophosphatidylserine (LysoPS) stimulation / treatment in CD4+ T cells and P2ry10/P2ry10b knockout vs wild-type in T cell-dependent colitis
incidental_ifn_note: Microbiota-derived metabolite LysoPS triggers metabolic reprogramming and drives IFN-gamma production in CD4+ Th1 cells in intestinal inflammation.
evidence: The study examines how microbiota-derived lysophosphatidylserine (LysoPS) induces metabolic reprogramming and pathological IFN-gamma-producing Th1 cell responses in mouse colitis.

title: Expression profiles of primary bone marrow derived mouse macrophages – untreated and treated with LPS or LPS+PGE
perturbation: LPS stimulation or LPS + prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) treatment vs untreated control in BMDMs
incidental_ifn_note: LPS stimulation of macrophages engages TLR4-TRIF signaling, which inherently induces type-I interferons and ISGs alongside inflammatory cytokines.
evidence: The dataset profiles bone marrow-derived macrophages treated with LPS or LPS+PGE2 to investigate macrophage polarization towards a regulatory anti-inflammatory phenotype.

title: Genome-wide gene expression profiling revealed a critical role for GATA3 in the maintenance of the Th2 cell identity
perturbation: GATA3 knockdown via siRNA transfection vs mock-transfected control in Th2 cells
incidental_ifn_note: siRNA knockdown transfection in cultured T cells can introduce exogenous RNA that may trigger low-level cytosolic RNA sensing or cellular stress.
evidence: The record profiles gene expression in Th2 cells following GATA3 siRNA knockdown to demonstrate GATA3 required role in maintaining Th2 cell lineage identity.

title: Bach2 inhibits Th2-type immune responses by regulating glutamine metabolism [expression array]
perturbation: Bach2 knockout (KO) vs wild-type (WT) in Th cells, with or without TCR restimulation
evidence: The record investigates how Bach2 represses glutaminase 2 expression and glutamine metabolism to regulate Th2 cell differentiation and allergic inflammation.

title: Tissue damage leads to a conserved stress response that initiates quiescent muscle stem cell activation
tissue_cell: skeletal muscle stem cells (satellite cells) and liver / muscle single nuclei
perturbation: Tissue injury / dissociation vs intact quiescent tissue
evidence: The record identifies a broadly conserved transcriptional stress response activated by tissue damage and enzymatic dissociation during quiescent muscle stem cell activation.

title: TCR repertoire analysis revealed the highly conserved TCR repertoire in the bilateral tumor in mice
tissue_cell: CD4+ and CD8+ tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) and draining lymph node T cells
perturbation: Bilateral Lewis lung carcinoma (LLC) subcutaneous tumor inoculation in C57BL/6 mice
evidence: The study analyzes TCR repertoires of CD4+ and CD8+ TILs and draining lymph node T cells in a bilateral Lewis lung carcinoma mouse model.

title: Effect of alisertib and navitoclax on gene expression in B16 melanoma tumors
perturbation: In vivo treatment with alisertib, navitoclax, or combination therapy vs vehicle control in B16 melanoma-bearing mice
incidental_ifn_note: Targeted kinase and apoptosis inhibitor therapies inducing tumor cell cytotoxicity can elicit secondary intratumoral inflammatory stress responses.
evidence: The record investigates RNA-seq gene expression responses of in vivo B16 melanoma tumors in mice treated with alisertib and navitoclax targeted therapies.

title: High throughput sequencing of immunoglobulin (Ig) heavy (IgH) and light (IgL) chain repertoires
tissue_cell: B cell subsets from bone marrow, spleen, and small intestinal lamina propria
perturbation: Comparison of Ig repertoires across B cell subsets in RAG2-GFP mice and germ-free vs SPF-colonized mice
evidence: The record sequences IgH and IgL chain repertoires of B cell subsets across tissues in RAG2-GFP reporter mice and germ-free versus colonized mice.

title: Multilayered control of alternative splicing regulatory networks by transcription factors
tissue_cell: Neuro2a (N2a) neuroblastoma cells and neural/stem cells
perturbation: Knockdown of transcription factors and splicing regulators (Zfp871, Nacc1, Mbnl1/2, Srrm4) vs non-targeting controls
incidental_ifn_note: ShRNA/siRNA transfection in neuroblastoma cells may cause low-level incidental cytosolic RNA activation or cellular stress.
evidence: The SuperSeries investigates how transcription factors (such as Zfp871 and Nacc1) systematically regulate alternative splicing networks in mouse neuroblastoma and stem cells.
